example.problem: Which coin is bigger: ₹1 or ₹10?
example.solution: ₹10 coin! It's worth ten times more than ₹1.

slides.inSimpleWords: Bigger numbers = coins worth more!

slides.title: Indian Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya pulls out paper money: 'Here's a red ₹10 note, then a blue-green ₹20 note, then a pink ₹50 note! Each worth more!'

points.label: Notes
points.text: ₹10 (red), ₹20 (blue-green), ₹50 (pink), ₹100 (green)

slides.inSimpleWords: Notes are colorful and worth more money!

slides.title: Comparing Note Values
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks: 'Is ₹20 worth more than ₹10?' Priya: 'Yes! ₹20 is twice ₹10. So one ₹20 note = two ₹10 notes!'

example.problem: Are ₹50 and ₹20 + ₹20 + ₹10 the same?

slides.inSimpleWords: Notes can be made from smaller notes!

slides.title: Counting Coins
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: 'I have 3 rupees in ₹1 coins, plus 1 rupee in a ₹5 coin... wait! That's just 1 rupee, not 5 rupees!'

example.problem: Count: three ₹1 coins + one ₹5 coin.

slides.inSimpleWords: Coins add up: 1+1+1+5 = 8 rupees.

slides.title: Counting Notes
slides.storyContext: Priya counts: 'One ₹50 note, one ₹20 note, one ₹10 note. That's 50 + 20 + 10 = 80 rupees!'

example.problem: Count: one ₹50 note + one ₹20 note + one ₹10 note.

slides.inSimpleWords: Notes add up quickly: 50+20+10 = 80.

slides.title: Mixed Money
slides.storyContext: Ravi now counts everything: '2 rupees in coins plus 80 rupees in notes. That's ₹82 total! Will it buy my sweets?'

points.label: All together
points.text: ₹8 (coins) + ₹80 (notes) = ₹88

slides.inSimpleWords: Count coins and notes together!

slides.title: Shopping at the Stall
slides.storyContext: The sweet seller says, 'Laddu is ₹10 each. Jalebi is ₹15 a plate. Kheer costs ₹20.' Ravi thinks hard!

example.problem: Ravi has ₹30. Can he buy 1 Jalebi (₹15) and 1 Kheer (₹20)?
example.solution: ₹15 + ₹20 = ₹35. No, he needs ₹5 more. He has only ₹30.

slides.inSimpleWords: Check prices before buying!

image.alt: Shopping at the Stall — Money Counting

slides.title: Making Change
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'If your ₹50 note pays for ₹30 worth of sweets, the seller gives you ₹20 change. 50 - 30 = 20!'

points.label: Change
points.text: Money given - Money spent = Change left

slides.inSimpleWords: Change is money you get back!

slides.title: Calculating Change
slides.storyContext: Ravi pays with ₹100 for ₹70 worth of sweets. 'How much change do I get?' Priya: '100 - 70 = 30 rupees!'

example.problem: Pay ₹100 for ₹70 sweets. Change?

slides.inSimpleWords: Change = Amount given - Cost!

slides.title: Real Purchase
slides.storyContext: Ravi buys 2 laddus (₹10 each) and 1 jalebi (₹15). He pays with ₹50. How much change?
slides.inSimpleWords: Ravi gets ₹15 back as change!

slides.title: Different Coins Make Same Value
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'Five ₹2 coins = 1 ₹10 coin. Same value, different coins!' Ravi's eyes light up.

example.problem: Are five ₹2 coins worth the same as one ₹10 coin?

slides.inSimpleWords: Different coins can make the same amount!

image.alt: Different Coins Make Same Value — Money Counting

slides.title: Budgeting: Plan Your Money
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'If you have ₹100, you can make a list: Sweets ₹40, Toys ₹30, Save ₹30. Plan before you spend!'

points.label: Smart spending
points.text: List items and prices. Add them up. Check if you have enough.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plan your spending before you buy!

slides.title: Budget Challenge
slides.storyContext: Ravi has ₹100. Wants: cookies ₹25, juice ₹20, toy ₹40. Can he buy all? '25+20+40 = 85. Yes! With ₹15 left!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Check totals and plan purchases!

slides.title: Money Combinations
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'To make ₹50, you could use: one ₹50 note, OR five ₹10 notes, OR two ₹20 notes and one ₹10 note!'

example.problem: Make ₹30 using ₹10 notes and ₹20 notes.
example.solution: Three ₹10 notes, OR one ₹20 note + one ₹10 note.

slides.inSimpleWords: Money can be made many ways!

slides.title: Shopping Mall Adventure
slides.storyContext: Ravi has ₹200. Book (₹50), Pen (₹20), Notebook (₹15), Snack (₹30). Total? '50+20+15+30=115. I have ₹85 left!'

points.label: Real scenario
points.text: Total spent: ₹115. Change: ₹200 - ₹115 = ₹85.

slides.inSimpleWords: Add prices, then find change!

slides.title: Skip Counting by 5s (Money Trick)
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches a trick: 'If counting ₹5 coins: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25! It's just like table of 5!' Ravi smiles: 'Multiplication helps money counting!'

example.problem: Count eight ₹5 coins.
example.solution: 8 × 5 = 40 rupees.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use multiplication to count money faster!

slides.title: Multiple Coins Practice
slides.storyContext: Ravi counts: '2 coins of ₹5 = 10, plus 3 coins of ₹2 = 6, plus 4 coins of ₹1 = 4. Total: 10 + 6 + 4 = 20 rupees!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Add all coins and notes together!

slides.title: Quick Counting with Multiplication
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'If you have 6 coins of ₹10, don't count 10+10+10+10+10+10. Just do 6×10=60!' Ravi smiles: 'Multiplication helps count money faster!'

points.label: Speed tip
points.text: Use multiplication when you have many of the same coin or note.

slides.inSimpleWords: Multiplication helps count money quickly!

slides.title: Exact Change Problem
slides.storyContext: At the market, Ravi buys items for ₹47. He gives ₹50. The seller says, 'Here's ₹3 change.' Ravi checks: '50 - 47 = 3. Yes! That's correct!'

points.label: Check change
points.text: Amount given (₹50) - Cost (₹47) = Change (₹3).

slides.inSimpleWords: Always verify your change!

slides.title: Saving Money
slides.storyContext: Ravi saves ₹20 per week. After 4 weeks, he has 4×20 = ₹80! 'Now I can buy that toy!' Priya nods: 'Saving adds up!'

example.problem: Save ₹20 per week for 4 weeks. Total?

slides.inSimpleWords: Saving money grows over time!

slides.title: Money in Real Life
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Money helps us buy food, clothes, toys, and books. We earn it by working and use it wisely by planning our spending.'

points.label: Using money
points.text: Money is earned, saved, and spent wisely for things we need and want.

slides.inSimpleWords: Money helps us live and have fun!

slides.title: Money Mastered!
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats his sweets happily. 'Priya, I know coins and notes now! Counting money is like counting numbers!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Indian coins: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10. 2. Indian notes: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100. 3. Add coins and notes together. 4. Check prices. 5. Calculate change. 6. Money math is number math!

slides.inSimpleWords: Money counting makes shopping easy!

subject: Mathematics
title: Ravi's Day Schedule
hook: Can Ravi read the clock to find time for all his favorite activities?

slides.title: Ravi Learns to Tell Time
slides.storyContext: Ravi walks into school and sees a big clock on the wall. He has so many questions about how it works.
slides.inSimpleWords: Today we learn to read clocks!

slides.title: What Time Is It?
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks at the big clock on his classroom wall. 'Priya, what do all these numbers and hands mean? I want to know when recess is!'

points.label: The clock
points.text: Clock has numbers 1-12 and two moving hands.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clocks tell us when things happen!

image.alt: What Time Is It? — Telling Time

slides.title: Priya's Promise
slides.storyContext: Priya smiles. 'Don't worry, Ravi! By the end of today, you'll be a clock expert. You'll know exactly when recess starts!'

points.label: What we'll learn
points.text: How the clock hands move, what the numbers mean, how to read hours and minutes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Learning to read time is fun and easy!

slides.title: The Clock Face
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'Look! There are 12 numbers around the clock. Top is 12. Right side is 3. Bottom is 6. Left is 9.'

points.label: Positions
points.text: 12 at top, 3 on right, 6 at bottom, 9 on left.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clock numbers are arranged in a circle!

slides.title: Why 12 Numbers?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Why 12?' Priya explains, 'A full day has 24 hours, but the clock shows 12 twice—morning and afternoon!'

points.label: Understanding 12
points.text: Clock shows 12 numbers. A.M. (morning): 12, 1, 2... 11. P.M. (afternoon/night): 12, 1, 2... 11.

slides.inSimpleWords: There are 12 hours shown, twice a day!

slides.title: The Two Hands
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'The short hand shows hours. The long hand shows minutes. Short moves slow, long moves fast!'

points.label: Hands
points.text: Short hand = hours, Long hand = minutes

slides.inSimpleWords: Short hand is hours, long hand is minutes.

slides.title: Ravi's Discovery
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches the long hand tick-tick-tick around the clock. 'Priya, it's moving!' Priya nods. 'Yes! It moves constantly. That's how we count minutes!'

points.label: Movement
points.text: The long hand moves around the whole clock in 60 minutes (one hour).

slides.inSimpleWords: The long hand moves to show minutes passing!

slides.title: Counting by 5s on a Clock
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches, 'Each big mark on the clock is 5 minutes. At 1: 5 min. At 2: 10 min. At 3: 15 min. We skip-count by 5s!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Numbers 1-12 also mean minutes by fives!

slides.title: Telling Hours
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'When the long hand points to 12 and the short hand points to 3, it's 3 o'clock!'

example.problem: If short hand is at 3 and long hand is at 12, what time is it?
example.solution: It is 3 o'clock (3:00).

slides.inSimpleWords: Short hand at 3, long hand at 12 = 3 o'clock.

slides.title: Another Hour
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees the short hand at 9 and long hand at 12. 'That's 9 o'clock! School time!' he shouts.

example.problem: Short hand at 9, long hand at 12. What time?
example.solution: It is 9 o'clock (9:00).

slides.inSimpleWords: 9 o'clock: short hand points to 9.

slides.title: One More Example
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'Short hand at 5, long hand at 12. That's 5 o'clock! Ravi, when do you usually have lunch?'

example.problem: Short hand at 5, long hand at 12. What time?
example.solution: It is 5 o'clock (5:00).

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading the hour: find the short hand!

slides.title: Reading Minutes
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Each small mark on the clock is one minute. 5 marks = 5 minutes. When the long hand is at 3, it's 15 minutes!'

points.label: Minutes
points.text: Long hand at 3 = 15 minutes. At 6 = 30 minutes. At 9 = 45 minutes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand shows: 0, 5, 10, 15... minutes.

slides.title: Ravi Practices
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches the long hand move from 12 to 1. 'It's been 5 minutes! I understand now!' He smiles at Priya.

points.label: Practice
points.text: After watching, Ravi can count forward by 5s on the clock.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice makes perfect!

slides.title: Quarter Past
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'When the long hand points to 3, it's quarter past! That's 15 minutes after the hour.'

example.problem: It's 4 o'clock. The long hand moves to 3. What time now?
example.solution: It is 4:15 (quarter past 4).

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand at 3 = quarter past (15 minutes).

slides.title: Half Past
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'When the long hand points to 6, it's half past the hour! Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes!'

example.problem: If it's 2 o'clock and the long hand moves to 6, what time is it now?
example.solution: It is 2:30 (half past 2, or 2 thirty).

slides.inSimpleWords: Long hand at 6 = half past (30 minutes).

slides.title: Quarter To (45 Minutes)
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'When the long hand points to 9, it's 45 minutes. We call this quarter to the next hour!'

points.label: Quarter to
points.text: Long hand at 9 = 45 minutes = quarter to next hour. Example: 2:45 = quarter to 3.

slides.inSimpleWords: Quarter to means 45 minutes past!

slides.title: Quarter To Example
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'It's 7:45. The short hand is between 7 and 8. The long hand is at 9. That's quarter to 8!'

example.problem: If short hand is between 3 and 4, and long hand is at 9, what time?
example.solution: It is 3:45 (quarter to 4).

slides.inSimpleWords: Three forty-five = quarter to four!

slides.title: Telling Time with Minutes
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches the full method: 'Look at the short hand first—that's hours. Then the long hand—that's minutes. Together they tell the whole time!'

points.label: Full time
points.text: Hours (short hand) + Minutes (long hand) = Complete time

slides.inSimpleWords: Short hand for hours, long hand for minutes!

slides.title: What Time Is It Now?
slides.storyContext: Priya asks Ravi to look at the classroom clock. Short hand at 10, long hand at 2. 'What time is it?' Ravi thinks... 'Ten and ten minutes!'

example.problem: Short hand at 10, long hand at 2. What time?
example.solution: It is 10:10 (ten ten, or ten minutes past ten).

slides.inSimpleWords: Find both hands, read the time!

slides.title: More Complex Times
slides.storyContext: Priya shows times: 'Look at this! Short hand at 6, long hand at 7. That's 6:35. Try another: short hand at 11, long hand at 4. That's 11:20!'

example.problem: Short hand at 8, long hand at 8. What time?
example.solution: It is 8:40 (eight forty, or eight and forty minutes).

slides.inSimpleWords: Keep practicing with different times!

slides.title: Ravi's Schedule
slides.storyContext: Priya writes Ravi's day on a board. 'School starts at 9:00. Recess at 11:00. Lunch at 1:00. Home at 3:00. You can now read all these times!'

points.label: Daily schedule
points.text: 9:00 - School starts. 11:00 - Recess. 1:00 - Lunch. 3:00 - Go home.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your day is planned by the clock!

slides.title: Ravi's Schedule
slides.storyContext: Priya writes Ravi's day: School starts at 9:00. Recess at 11:00. Lunch at 1:00. Home at 3:00. 'Read each time on the clock!'

points.label: Schedule
points.text: 9:00 - School. 11:00 - Recess. 1:00 - Lunch. 3:00 - Home.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clocks help us organize our day!

slides.title: How Long Does Recess Last?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Priya, recess is at 11:00. When does it end?' Priya replies, 'Usually 30 minutes. So it ends at 11:30!'

points.label: Duration
points.text: Time + Duration = End time. Example: Start 11:00 + 30 minutes = End 11:30.

slides.inSimpleWords: We can add time to find when things end!

slides.title: What Time for Play?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'If school ends at 3:00 and play time is half an hour later, what time is play?' Priya helps: 3:00 + 30 minutes = 3:30!

example.problem: School ends at 3:00. If you have 20 minutes to walk home, what time do you arrive?

slides.inSimpleWords: Add minutes to know future times!

slides.title: What Time for Play?
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'If school ends at 3:00 and play time is half an hour later, what time is play?' Priya helps: 3:00 + 30 minutes = 3:30!
slides.inSimpleWords: Add minutes to know future times!

image.alt: What Time for Play? — Telling Time

slides.title: A.M. vs P.M.
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'A.M. means morning (before noon). P.M. means afternoon and night (after noon). 9:00 A.M. is morning school. 9:00 P.M. is bedtime!'

points.label: A.M. and P.M.
points.text: A.M. = morning (12:00 - 11:59). P.M. = afternoon/evening (12:00 - 11:59)

slides.inSimpleWords: A.M. is morning, P.M. is afternoon/night!

slides.title: Time Mastered!
slides.storyContext: Ravi now reads the clock easily. 'I know hours and minutes! I can find time for school, recess, lunch, and play!'

points.label: Review
points.text: 1. Clock has 12 numbers. 2. Short hand = hours. 3. Long hand = minutes. 4. At 12 = top of hour. 5. At 3 = quarter past (15 min). 6. At 6 = half past (30 min). 7. At 9 = quarter to (45 min).

slides.inSimpleWords: Reading a clock helps plan your day!

slides.title: Real-World Clock Challenge
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Ravi homework. 'Tomorrow, tell me what time you wake up, eat breakfast, start school, have recess, eat lunch, and go to bed. Use your clock!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Track your own daily times using a real clock.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use your new skills every single day!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya's Garden Discovery
hook: What makes a plant different from a stone?

slides.title: Living vs Non-Living
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya step into a beautiful garden full of mysteries waiting to be discovered.
slides.inSimpleWords: Let's explore nature's two big groups!

slides.title: The Garden Walk
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya walk into Priya's garden. 'Ravi, look around! This garden has living things and non-living things. Can you spot them?'

points.label: The garden
points.text: Plants, insects, stones, water, soil, and more!

slides.inSimpleWords: Nature has living AND non-living things.

image.alt: The Garden Walk — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: First Observation
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks around confused. 'How do we tell which is which?' Priya smiles. 'Let me teach you the secret signs of life!'

points.label: What we'll learn
points.text: Key differences between living and non-living things.

slides.inSimpleWords: Everything has signs that tell us if it's alive!

slides.title: What Are Living Things?
slides.storyContext: Priya picks a green plant. 'This plant grows! It needs water, sunlight, and soil. It's alive! We call it a living thing.'

points.label: Living things
points.text: Grow, need food/water, can move, make babies, breathe.

slides.inSimpleWords: Living things grow and need food!

image.alt: What Are Living Things? — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Five Signs of Life
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'There are five main signs that something is alive: 1) Grows bigger. 2) Eats food. 3) Breathes. 4) Moves. 5) Makes babies!'

points.label: Five signs
points.text: Growth, feeding/eating, breathing, movement, reproduction

slides.inSimpleWords: Living things show all five signs!

slides.title: Ravi Tests Each Sign
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks at the plant. 'It gets bigger! It drinks water! Its leaves move in the wind! But... does it breathe like me?' Priya nods. 'Yes, through tiny holes in leaves!'

points.label: Plant proof
points.text: Plants show all five signs in their own way.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants are definitely alive!

slides.title: Plants Are Living
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees tomato plants with red tomatoes. 'Priya, look! The flowers became tomatoes! Plants make babies!'

example.problem: Why is a tomato plant living?
example.solution: It grows, needs water, makes fruits (babies), and breathes through leaves.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants are living because they grow!

image.alt: Plants Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Animals Are Living
slides.storyContext: A butterfly lands on the flower. 'See this butterfly? It eats, it moves, it breathes. Animals are living things too!'

points.label: Animals
points.text: Eat food, move around, breathe, have babies, feel things.

slides.inSimpleWords: Animals are living because they move and eat!

image.alt: Animals Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Watch the Butterfly
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches the butterfly sip nectar from a flower. 'It's eating!' Then it flies away. 'And moving! Is it breathing too?' Priya nods excitedly.

points.label: Signs of life
points.text: The butterfly eats, moves, breathes—all signs of life!

slides.inSimpleWords: The butterfly shows it's alive!

slides.title: More Animals
slides.storyContext: Ravi finds an ant carrying food. An earthworm in the soil. A sparrow singing. 'So many living animals!'

example.problem: Are ants, worms, and birds living things?
example.solution: Yes! They all eat, move, breathe, and have babies. They are living.

slides.inSimpleWords: Ants, worms, birds all are living!

slides.title: What Are Non-Living Things?
slides.storyContext: Priya picks up a stone. 'Now look at this rock. It doesn't grow. It doesn't eat. It doesn't move by itself. This is non-living.'

points.label: Non-living things
points.text: Don't grow, don't need food, don't breathe, don't move by themselves.

slides.inSimpleWords: Non-living things don't grow or eat!

image.alt: What Are Non-Living Things? — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Testing the Stone
slides.storyContext: Ravi holds the stone. 'It's hard and cold. It never grows bigger... or eats... or moves on its own!' Priya says, 'Exactly! It shows zero signs of life!'

points.label: Stone proof
points.text: A stone has none of the five signs of life.

slides.inSimpleWords: Stones are definitely not alive!

slides.title: Other Non-Living Things
slides.storyContext: Priya points around. 'Non-living things are everywhere: water, soil, air, wood, metal, glass, plastic, paper. Anything without life signs is non-living!'

points.label: Examples
points.text: Water, air, soil, metals, plastics, wood (after cut), rocks, sand.

slides.inSimpleWords: Many things around us are non-living!

slides.title: Water and Soil
slides.storyContext: Ravi fills a bucket with water from the well. Priya says, 'Water and soil are non-living. We use them, but they're not alive.'

example.problem: Is water living or non-living?
example.solution: Water is non-living. It doesn't grow or eat, but plants need it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water and soil are non-living helpers!

image.alt: Water and Soil — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Once Alive, Now Non-Living
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a piece of wood. 'This wood came from a tree—once alive! But the tree was cut down. Now the wood is non-living.'

points.label: Dead vs non-living
points.text: Dead things are non-living. They once lived but no longer show life signs.

slides.inSimpleWords: Things can stop being alive!

slides.title: Spot the Difference
slides.storyContext: Priya points to different things. 'That tree? Living. That wood chair? Non-living, because the tree is cut down now.'

points.label: Learning
points.text: Wood from a tree becomes a chair (non-living once cut).

slides.inSimpleWords: Cut wood stops being alive!

image.alt: Spot the Difference — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Humans Are Living
slides.storyContext: Ravi points to himself. 'Are we living things, Priya?' She nods. 'Yes! You eat, breathe, grow, and move. You're very alive!'

example.problem: Is a human a living thing?
example.solution: Yes! Humans grow, eat, breathe, feel, and have children. We are the most complex living things!

slides.inSimpleWords: We are living things too!

image.alt: Humans Are Living — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Ravi's Big Discovery
slides.storyContext: Ravi realizes, 'So in this garden, the butterfly, ant, worm, bird, plant, tree, and even us—we're all LIVING. But the rock, water, soil, air, and wood—NON-LIVING!'

points.label: Understanding
points.text: Living things and non-living things coexist in nature.

slides.inSimpleWords: Living and non-living work together!

slides.title: They Need Each Other
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Living things need non-living things to survive! Plants need water and soil. Animals need air and water. They all depend on each other!'

points.label: Interdependence
points.text: Living things depend on non-living things, and vice versa, for survival.

slides.inSimpleWords: Living and non-living need each other!

slides.title: Make Two Lists
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Ravi, let's make a list. Living: plants, butterflies, ants, worms, birds, us. Non-living: stones, water, soil, air, wood, plastic.'

points.label: Organizing
points.text: Living and non-living both are part of nature!

slides.inSimpleWords: We can sort things into two groups!

image.alt: Make Two Lists — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Spot It in Your Home
slides.storyContext: Priya gives homework. 'Go home and find 5 living and 5 non-living things. Write or draw them. We'll compare tomorrow!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Identify living and non-living around you daily.

slides.inSimpleWords: Hunt for examples everywhere!

slides.title: Microorganisms—Tiny Living Things
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Some living things are SO tiny we can't see them without a microscope. Bacteria in soil help plants! Mold grows on food!'

points.label: Microscopic life
points.text: Bacteria, fungi, microbes are living but invisible to eyes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some living things are too tiny to see!

slides.title: Garden Lesson Complete
slides.storyContext: As the sun sets, Ravi and Priya sit. 'Everything in this garden—plants, animals, stones, water—works together. The living needs the non-living!'

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Living things grow, eat, breathe, move. 2. Non-living things don't. 3. Both are important. 4. Together they make nature beautiful. 5. We are living and part of nature!

slides.inSimpleWords: Living things and non-living things work together!

image.alt: Garden Lesson Complete — Living and Non-Living

slides.title: Five Signs Memory Test
slides.storyContext: Priya quizzes Ravi. 'Name five signs of life.' Ravi shouts, 'Growth, eating, breathing, movement, and making babies!'

points.label: Recall
points.text: The five signs: Grow, Eat, Breathe, Move, Reproduce

slides.inSimpleWords: Remember the five signs of life!

slides.title: Mystery Object Game
slides.storyContext: Priya holds up random things: a pen, a leaf, a pebble, a beetle. 'Is it living or non-living? Why?' Ravi answers each.

points.label: Assessment
points.text: Apply the five signs to decide if something is alive or not.

slides.inSimpleWords: Test your new knowledge!

slides.title: Treasure Hunt
slides.storyContext: Priya challenges Ravi with a final quest. 'This week, find three living things in your home and three non-living things. Explain to your family WHY each one is alive or not alive!'

points.label: Real-world mastery
points.text: Apply learning to daily observations and explain to others.

slides.inSimpleWords: Teach others what you learned!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi and Priya's Animal Adventure
hook: Where does a bird sleep? Where does a fish rest?

slides.title: Animal Homes & Habitats
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya embark on an exciting journey to discover where different animals live and why.
slides.inSimpleWords: Let's explore where animals live!

slides.title: Different Houses, Different Animals
slides.storyContext: Ravi and Priya explore nature. 'Priya, do all animals live in the same kind of home?' Priya smiles. 'No! Each animal has its own perfect home!'

points.label: Discovery
points.text: Animals live in different places based on what they need.

slides.inSimpleWords: Different animals have different homes!

image.alt: Different Houses, Different Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: A Question About Homes
slides.storyContext: Ravi wonders aloud, 'Why don't all animals live in houses like we do?' Priya explains, 'Because each animal's body is designed for its own special home!'

points.label: Adaptation
points.text: Animals' bodies fit their homes perfectly.

slides.inSimpleWords: Each animal is perfect for its home!

slides.title: Nests for Birds
slides.storyContext: Priya points to a nest in a tree. 'See this nest? Birds build it from twigs and grass. They lay eggs here and raise babies!'

points.label: Bird homes
points.text: Birds live in nests in trees, bushes, rocks, or holes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Birds make nests in trees!

image.alt: Nests for Birds — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Why Nests?
slides.storyContext: Ravi touches a nest gently. 'Why is this shape? Why use twigs?' Priya answers, 'The cup shape holds eggs safe. Twigs are strong. The high tree keeps eggs from predators!'

points.label: Design
points.text: Nests are shaped and positioned to protect eggs and chicks.

slides.inSimpleWords: Nests are built smart!

slides.title: Different Bird Nests
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees many nests. 'Some are round, some are messy, some are tiny!' Priya says, 'Each bird builds its own style of nest!'

example.problem: Where does a sparrow sleep?
example.solution: In a nest made of grass and twigs in a tree or on a building.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sparrows nest in trees and buildings!

image.alt: Different Bird Nests — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Holes for Small Animals
slides.storyContext: Priya shows a burrow in the ground. 'Rabbits and squirrels dig holes called burrows. Underground is safe and cool!'

points.label: Underground homes
points.text: Rabbits, squirrels, moles, and frogs live in holes and burrows.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some animals dig holes underground!

image.alt: Holes for Small Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Exploring a Burrow
slides.storyContext: Ravi peers into a rabbit hole. 'It's so deep! How far does it go?' Priya explains, 'Tunnels go many feet down, with rooms for sleeping, storing food, and hiding from danger!'

points.label: Burrow design
points.text: Burrows have multiple chambers (rooms) for different purposes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Burrows have many rooms!

slides.title: Ant Hill and Beehive
slides.storyContext: Ravi finds an anthill. 'Look at all those tunnels!' Then Priya shows a beehive in a tree. 'Ants and bees build amazing homes together!'

example.problem: Where do ants live?
example.solution: In anthills with tunnels underground. Many ants live and work together.

slides.inSimpleWords: Ants live in hills; bees live in hives!

image.alt: Ant Hill and Beehive — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Team Homes
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Ants and bees don't live alone. Hundreds work together! They have a queen, workers, and guards. The hive/hill is their city!'

points.label: Social homes
points.text: Ants and bees live in colonies. Each has a role: queen, workers, soldiers.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some animals build homes together!

slides.title: Water Homes
slides.storyContext: They visit a pond. Priya says, 'Fish live in water. Frogs also live here. Even snakes can hide in water!'

points.label: Aquatic homes
points.text: Fish, frogs, turtles, and water snakes live in ponds, rivers, lakes.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fish and frogs live in water!

image.alt: Water Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Water Is Their World
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches fish glide through water. 'They don't need a nest or hole! Water IS their home!' Priya nods. 'Right! Fish have gills to breathe underwater. Perfect adaptation!'

points.label: Water adaptation
points.text: Aquatic animals have bodies made for water: gills, fins, shells.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water animals are built for water!

slides.title: Shells and Coral Homes
slides.storyContext: Priya shows a snail shell. 'This snail carries its home! Crabs have hard shells too. In the sea, fish hide in coral!'

example.problem: Where does a snail live?
example.solution: In its hard shell, which it carries everywhere as protection.

slides.inSimpleWords: Snails carry their homes!

image.alt: Shells and Coral Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Protective Shells
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'A snail's shell grows with it! It protects the soft body inside. Crabs and turtles have shells too—nature's armor!'

points.label: Shells
points.text: Shells are built-in homes that protect from predators and weather.

slides.inSimpleWords: Shells are living homes!

slides.title: Dens and Caves
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Do big animals like lions live in homes too?' Priya nods. 'Lions live in caves or dens. Tigers hide in forests. Elephants roam wide areas.'

points.label: Big homes
points.text: Lions: caves/dens. Tigers: forests. Elephants: grasslands.

slides.inSimpleWords: Big animals live in caves and forests!

image.alt: Dens and Caves — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Roaming Habitats
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches, 'Not all animals have one home. Elephants and tigers roam huge areas called territories. Each territory has food, water, and safety.'

points.label: Territories
points.text: Large animals roam territories (ranges). They need space to hunt and live.

slides.inSimpleWords: Big animals roam wide territories!

slides.title: Homes Protect Animals
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Homes keep animals safe from danger. Nests keep baby birds warm. Burrows keep rabbits from predators.'

example.problem: Why does a rabbit live in a burrow?
example.solution: Underground is safe from predators and keeps them cool in summer, warm in winter.

slides.inSimpleWords: Homes keep animals safe and comfy!

image.alt: Homes Protect Animals — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Homes Have Jobs
slides.storyContext: Priya summarizes, 'Animal homes do many things: protect from danger, keep warm/cool, store food, raise babies, hide from weather. Different homes fit different needs!'

points.label: Home purposes
points.text: Protection, shelter, food storage, breeding, rest.

slides.inSimpleWords: Homes do many important jobs!

slides.title: Match Animals to Homes
slides.storyContext: Ravi tries to match: 'Sparrow → nest, fish → water, squirrel → hole, lion → cave!' Priya claps, 'Perfect!'

points.label: Practice
points.text: Different animals, different homes. All perfectly suited!

slides.inSimpleWords: Each animal picks the best home!

image.alt: Match Animals to Homes — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Build a Home
slides.storyContext: Priya asks, 'If YOU were a bird, how would you build a nest? Where? With what?' Ravi imagines and shares ideas.

points.label: Thinking
points.text: Think about what animal needs in a home: safety, warmth, space, resources.

slides.inSimpleWords: Design homes like an engineer!

slides.title: Seasonal Homes
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Some animals change homes with seasons! Birds migrate (fly) to warmer places in winter. Squirrels nest up trees in summer, but deeper holes in winter!'

points.label: Seasonal shifts
points.text: Animals adapt homes or move homes based on weather and food availability.

slides.inSimpleWords: Animals switch homes when seasons change!

slides.title: Animal Homes Tour Ends
slides.storyContext: As they walk home, Ravi realizes, 'Every animal has a home made just for it! Birds in nests, fish in water, rabbits in holes. Nature is amazing!'

points.label: Learning
points.text: 1. Birds live in nests. 2. Small animals in burrows/holes. 3. Fish and frogs in water. 4. Big animals in caves/forests. 5. Homes keep animals safe. 6. Each home is perfectly suited to that animal!

slides.inSimpleWords: Every animal has a perfect home!

image.alt: Animal Homes Tour Ends — Animals and Their Homes

slides.title: Habitat Hunt at Home
slides.storyContext: Priya gives homework. 'Find animal homes near your house: bird nests, spider webs, ant hills, insect holes. Take photos or draw them!'

points.label: Real-world exploration
points.text: Observe real animal homes in your neighborhood.

slides.inSimpleWords: Look for animal homes everywhere!

slides.title: Types and Reasons Quiz
slides.storyContext: Priya asks, 'Why do birds build nests in trees instead of on the ground?' Ravi answers, 'Safety! Up high keeps babies from predators!'

points.label: Understanding
points.text: Each home type exists because of the animal's needs and dangers.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every design has a reason!

slides.title: Draw Your Own Animal Home
slides.storyContext: Priya challenges Ravi, 'Invent a new animal. What would its home look like? Where would it live? Why?' Ravi sketches excitedly.

points.label: Creativity & reasoning
points.text: Apply learned concepts to imagine new animal-habitat pairs.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use your imagination!

slides.title: Animal Detective
slides.storyContext: Priya gives final homework. 'Find 5 animals near you this week. For each one, answer: Where does it live? What does its home protect it from? What does it need in a home?'

points.label: Real-world research
points.text: Observe and document animals and their habitats locally.

slides.inSimpleWords: Be a nature detective!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Priya's Water Adventure
hook: Where does rain go? Where does it come from?

slides.title: Following a Water Droplet
slides.storyContext: Priya asks Ravi, 'Have you ever wondered where rainwater goes? Let's follow one water droplet on a magical journey!'

points.label: The journey
points.text: Water evaporates, condenses, precipitates, and returns—over and over!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water travels in a never-ending circle!

image.alt: Following a Water Droplet — Water Cycle

slides.title: A Droplet's Name
slides.storyContext: Priya says, 'Let's call this water droplet Drippy! Drippy starts in the ocean, minding his own business. Then the sun appears—and that's when his adventure begins!'

points.label: Character setup
points.text: Drippy the water droplet begins in the vast ocean with billions of other water molecules.

slides.inSimpleWords: Meet Drippy, our water droplet hero!

slides.title: The Water Cycle Overview
slides.storyContext: Priya draws a circle on paper. 'The water cycle has four main steps: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, and Collection. Then it starts again! Forever and ever!'

points.label: Four steps
points.text: Evaporation (water rises), Condensation (clouds form), Precipitation (rain falls), Collection (water gathers), then repeat.

slides.inSimpleWords: Four steps, round and round!

slides.title: Evaporation: Water Rises
slides.storyContext: Priya washes clothes in the sun. 'Watch the wet cloth get dry! The sun heats water and turns it invisible. It floats up as vapor!'

points.label: Evaporation
points.text: Sun heats water. Water becomes invisible steam and rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Sun turns water into invisible steam!

slides.title: Water Evaporates Everywhere
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees puddles on the road after rain. 'Priya, where do the puddles go?' She smiles. 'The sun evaporates them! See how they disappear?'

example.problem: What happens to puddles on a sunny day?
example.solution: The sun heats them and turns the water into invisible vapor that rises into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: Puddles disappear because sun evaporates water!

slides.title: Drippy Rises
slides.storyContext: The sun heats the ocean. Drippy feels warm energy. 'What's happening?' he wonders. His friend Water tells him, 'We're being evaporated! We're turning into invisible vapor and floating upward into the sky!'

points.label: Evaporation begins
points.text: Solar heat provides energy. Water molecules gain energy and escape as vapor.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy transforms into invisible vapor and floats up!

slides.title: Heat Energy Powers Evaporation
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Why doesn't water evaporate when it's cold?' Priya explains, 'Heat is the key! The sun's warmth gives energy to water molecules, making them rise.'

points.label: Heat energy
points.text: Evaporation needs energy from the sun. Heat makes water molecules move fast and escape into the air.

slides.inSimpleWords: No heat, no evaporation—the sun is the engine!

slides.title: Ocean Water Evaporates Most
slides.storyContext: Priya takes Ravi to a lake and points outward. 'Most water on Earth is in the oceans. Billions of liters evaporate every day from the sun's heat. This is the biggest source of water vapor!'

points.label: Ocean evaporation
points.text: The ocean is Earth's biggest water source. Millions of tons evaporate daily.

slides.inSimpleWords: Oceans give us most of the water vapor in the air!

slides.title: Evaporation Rate
slides.storyContext: Ravi wonders, 'How fast does water evaporate?' Priya says, 'On a hot sunny day, a puddle can vanish in hours. In winter, it takes much longer. Temperature is the key!'

example.problem: Why do puddles disappear faster on hot days than cold days?
example.solution: Hot days provide more solar energy. More energy means faster evaporation. Cold days have less energy, so evaporation is slower.

slides.inSimpleWords: Heat speed = evaporation speed!

slides.title: Condensation: Water Cools
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a cold glass of water on a warm day. 'See these droplets on the outside? Cold air turns vapor back into liquid water!'

points.label: Condensation
points.text: Vapor cools down high in the sky and turns back into tiny water droplets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cool air turns steam back into water!

slides.title: Drippy's Long Journey Up
slides.storyContext: High in the sky, Drippy floats as invisible vapor. He gets tired, floating higher and higher. 'How much longer?' he sighs. Priya explains, 'He's rising to where it's very cold. Soon he'll meet his friends again!'

points.label: Rising vapor
points.text: Water vapor rises high into the atmosphere, away from the warm surface.

slides.inSimpleWords: Vapor rises higher and higher!

slides.title: Clouds Form
slides.storyContext: Ravi looks up at the sky. Priya explains, 'Those clouds are made of millions of tiny water droplets! They formed when vapor cooled high up!'

example.problem: What are clouds made of?
example.solution: Clouds are millions of tiny water droplets formed when water vapor cools.

slides.inSimpleWords: Clouds are cooled water vapor!

slides.title: Temperature Drop Creates Condensation
slides.storyContext: Priya points upward. 'Water vapor rises higher and higher. The higher up, the colder it gets. When vapor reaches cold air, it condenses and forms clouds!'

points.label: Temperature drop
points.text: Air gets colder as you go higher. At high altitude, vapor hits cold air and condenses.

slides.inSimpleWords: Higher up equals colder equals clouds!

slides.title: Drippy Condenses
slides.storyContext: High in the cold sky, Drippy shivers. 'Brr!' He bumps into other vapor molecules. 'Come together!' says an older droplet. They merge, growing heavier. Drippy becomes visible again—a tiny cloud droplet!

points.label: Condensation moment
points.text: As vapor cools, water molecules slow down and stick together, forming visible liquid droplets.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy becomes solid again inside a cloud!

slides.title: Cloud Types Tell Stories
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees fluffy white clouds, thin wispy clouds, and dark gray clouds. Priya says, 'Different clouds mean different weather. Thick dark clouds bring heavy rain!'

points.label: Cloud formation
points.text: Clouds come in different shapes and sizes. Thick clouds hold more water droplets and bring rain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Cloud colors and shapes predict weather!

slides.title: Precipitation: Rain Falls
slides.storyContext: Dark clouds gather. 'Now watch!' says Priya. Rain begins to fall! 'The droplets are so heavy they fall as rain. That's precipitation!'

points.label: Precipitation
points.text: When cloud droplets get too heavy, they fall as rain (or snow, or hail).

slides.inSimpleWords: Heavy droplets fall as rain!

slides.title: Why Rain Falls
slides.storyContext: Ravi wonders, 'Why do clouds suddenly drop rain?' Priya explains, 'Droplets bump into each other and merge, getting heavier. Eventually they're too heavy to float. Gravity pulls them down!'

example.problem: What makes raindrops fall from clouds?
example.solution: Water droplets collide and combine inside clouds, growing heavier until gravity pulls them down as rain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Droplets merge, get heavy, then fall!

slides.title: Different Types of Precipitation
slides.storyContext: Priya explains to Ravi: 'In India, we mostly see rain. But in very cold places, precipitation falls as snow or sleet or hail. It's all water, just in different forms!'

points.label: Precipitation forms
points.text: Rain (warm), snow (freezing), hail (ice pellets), sleet (mixed). All are water falling from clouds.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water falls in many forms depending on temperature!

slides.title: Drippy Falls as Rain
slides.storyContext: Inside the dark cloud, Drippy and trillions of friends have merged into heavy raindrops. They can't float anymore. Down they come! 'Here we go!' shouts Drippy. Splash! Rain pours on Ravi's village!

points.label: Rainfall
points.text: Billions of water droplets fall together as rain, replenishing rivers and soil.

slides.inSimpleWords: Drippy's grand descent begins!

slides.title: Rain on Land
slides.storyContext: Rain pours down. Ravi sees it trickling into the ground, filling wells, ponds, and rivers. 'Where does all this water go?'

example.problem: Where does rainwater go after it falls?
example.solution: Some soaks into the ground (groundwater), some flows into rivers and ponds, some is drunk by plants and animals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain soaks into ground and fills rivers!

slides.title: Water Soaks Deep
slides.storyContext: Priya kneels in wet soil. 'Some rain doesn't stay on the surface. It soaks down through soil and rock. This becomes groundwater—water that plants and underground streams use!'

points.label: Infiltration
points.text: Rainwater soaks into soil and rock, becoming groundwater. It fills wells and aquifers.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rain sinks into Earth's deep ground!

slides.title: Collection: Water Gathers
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a well, a pond, and the river. 'Look! All this water came from rain. It collects here, waiting to be used.'

points.label: Collection
points.text: Rainwater collects in wells, rivers, lakes, and oceans—the water cycle starts again!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water collects in rivers and ponds!

slides.title: Groundwater to Plants
slides.storyContext: Ravi sees plant roots going deep into soil. Priya explains, 'Plant roots drink groundwater! They pull it up from underground to grow and make leaves. This water will eventually evaporate too!'

example.problem: How do plants get water in dry seasons?
example.solution: Plant roots extend deep underground to reach groundwater. They absorb it and use it to grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants drink groundwater through their roots!

slides.title: Transpiration: Plants Release Water
slides.storyContext: Priya points to leaves glistening in the morning sun. 'Plants don't just store water. They release water vapor through tiny holes in leaves called stomata. This is called transpiration!'

points.label: Transpiration
points.text: Plants absorb groundwater and release water vapor through leaves. This vapor goes back into the atmosphere!

slides.inSimpleWords: Plants release water vapor into the air!

slides.title: Drippy in the Well
slides.storyContext: Drippy lands in Ravi's village well. 'Another adventure!' he thinks. Ravi's family draws water from the well. 'Drippy is giving us life-giving water!' Ravi declares. But Drippy's journey isn't over—the cycle continues forever.

points.label: Drippy's pause
points.text: Water collects in wells and is used by humans, but it will evaporate again and again.

slides.inSimpleWords: Even used water will cycle again!

slides.title: The Complete Cycle
slides.storyContext: Priya draws a circle. 'Evaporation → Condensation → Precipitation → Collection → Evaporation again! It never stops!'

points.label: Cycle
points.text: The water cycle is continuous and endless.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water goes round and round forever!

slides.title: Cycle Challenge: Label Each Step
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Ravi a challenge: 'I'll describe each step. You name it! (1) Water vapor rises. (2) Clouds form. (3) Rain falls. (4) Water collects in rivers.' Ravi correctly answers: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection!

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Can you name each stage of the water cycle?

slides.inSimpleWords: Four stages, five words: Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, Collection, Repeat!

slides.title: Same Water, Always
slides.storyContext: Ravi realizes, 'So the rain that falls today might have been in this well before!' Priya nods. 'Yes! Same water, recycled forever!'

example.problem: Is the water we drink the same water from millions of years ago?
example.solution: Yes! Earth's water is recycled endlessly through the water cycle.

slides.inSimpleWords: Same water gets reused forever!

slides.title: Water Journey Ends
slides.storyContext: That night, Ravi watches the rain. He now knows each droplet's journey—up, into clouds, down as rain, and starting again!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Evaporation: Sun heats water into vapor. 2. Condensation: Vapor cools into droplets. 3. Precipitation: Droplets fall as rain. 4. Collection: Water gathers in rivers/ponds. 5. The cycle repeats forever! 6. All water is recycled. 7. Plants help the cycle via transpiration. 8. We must protect this precious cycle.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water cycles through evaporation, clouds, and rain!

subject: The World Around Us
title: Ravi and Priya's Healthy Plate
hook: Which foods make us strong and which make us sick?

slides.title: Mummy's Kitchen Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi comes home tired. His mother makes him a meal with rice, beans, vegetables, and fruit. Priya visits and says, 'Your mom is teaching you about healthy eating!'

points.label: The meal
points.text: Different foods give different nutrients to our body.

slides.inSimpleWords: Healthy food gives us energy and strength!

slides.title: Energy for Playing
slides.storyContext: Ravi is too tired to play cricket. Priya asks, 'Did you eat breakfast?' He shakes his head. 'That's the problem! Food is fuel for your body, just like petrol for a car. No fuel, no energy!'

points.label: Food as fuel
points.text: Food gives energy to run, play, think, and grow. Without food, we feel tired.

slides.inSimpleWords: Food is fuel for our bodies!

slides.title: What is Nutrition?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Our food breaks down into tiny nutrients—proteins, carbs, fats, vitamins, minerals, water. Each does a special job in our body!'

points.label: Nutrients
points.text: Carbs give energy. Proteins build muscles. Fats store energy. Vitamins and minerals keep us healthy.

slides.inSimpleWords: Different nutrients do different jobs in our body!

slides.title: Six Main Food Groups
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a chart: Grains, Proteins, Vegetables, Fruits, Dairy, and Fats. 'Every food belongs to one of these groups. Each group has special powers!'

points.label: Food groups
points.text: Grains (energy), Proteins (growth), Vegetables (vitamins), Fruits (immunity), Dairy (bones), Healthy Fats (brain).

slides.inSimpleWords: Six food groups, six superpowers!

slides.title: Grains for Energy
slides.storyContext: Priya points to rice and bread. 'These are grains. They give your body energy so you can run, play, and study hard!'

points.label: Grains
points.text: Rice, wheat, bread, roti—give energy and strength.

slides.inSimpleWords: Grains give us energy to play!

slides.title: Carbohydrates Explained
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Priya, how do grains give energy?' She explains, 'Grains have carbohydrates. When you eat them, your body breaks them down into glucose—sugar that becomes instant energy!'

example.problem: How does eating rice give us energy?
example.solution: Rice contains carbohydrates. Our body breaks them down into glucose, which enters our blood and powers our muscles and brain.

slides.inSimpleWords: Carbs turn into sugar that powers us!

slides.title: Protein for Growing
slides.storyContext: Priya shows beans, eggs, and paneer. 'These have protein. Protein helps you grow tall and makes your muscles strong!'

points.label: Protein
points.text: Beans, eggs, milk, yogurt, paneer, fish—build muscles and make you grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Protein helps us grow tall and strong!

slides.title: Building Blocks
slides.storyContext: Ravi watches a construction site. Priya points, 'See how workers stack bricks? Protein builds your body the same way! Each protein molecule is a brick in your muscles and bones.'

example.problem: Why do growing children need protein?
example.solution: Protein provides amino acids that build muscle tissue, bone, and other body structures. Growing kids need lots of it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Protein builds muscles and bones!

slides.title: Vegetables for Vitamins
slides.storyContext: Priya holds green leafy vegetables, orange carrots, red tomatoes. 'Each color gives different vitamins. Green keeps eyes healthy, orange is good for seeing!'

points.label: Vegetables
points.text: Carrots, spinach, tomatoes, peas—full of vitamins and minerals.

slides.inSimpleWords: Colorful veggies keep us healthy!

slides.title: Rainbow Vegetables
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Ravi: 'Green veggies have folate for blood. Orange has beta-carotene for eyes. Red has lycopene for heart. Eat the rainbow!'

points.label: Color equals nutrients
points.text: Each color vegetable has unique vitamins. Eating many colors keeps all body parts healthy.

slides.inSimpleWords: Colorful vegetables give different health benefits!

slides.title: Key Vitamins and Minerals
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a chart. 'Vitamin A helps eyes. Vitamin C helps immunity. Iron helps blood. Calcium helps bones. All found in different vegetables!'

points.label: Key nutrients
points.text: Vitamin A (carrots, spinach), Vitamin C (tomatoes, peppers), Iron (spinach), Calcium (milk, greens).

slides.inSimpleWords: Each vitamin does a special job!

slides.title: Fruits for Immunity
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats an apple and banana. Priya explains, 'Fruits have vitamins that keep you from getting sick. Eat different colored fruits!'

example.problem: Why should we eat fruits daily?
example.solution: Fruits have vitamins that boost immunity and prevent sickness. Oranges have vitamin C, bananas have potassium.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits keep our bodies strong!

slides.title: Natural Sweets vs Junk Sweets
slides.storyContext: Ravi wants to eat candy. Priya offers him a banana. 'Both are sweet, but banana has fiber, potassium, and vitamins. Candy has only sugar and empty calories. Banana is smarter!'

points.label: Better choices
points.text: Natural sweets (fruits) have nutrients. Candy and sweets have only sugar.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fruits are sweet AND healthy!

slides.title: Dairy for Bones
slides.storyContext: Priya pours milk. 'Milk, yogurt, and paneer have calcium. Calcium makes your bones and teeth strong and healthy!'

points.label: Dairy
points.text: Milk, yogurt, cheese—calcium for strong bones and teeth.

slides.inSimpleWords: Milk makes bones strong!

slides.title: Calcium in Detail
slides.storyContext: Ravi asks, 'Why is calcium so important?' Priya explains, 'Calcium makes bones hard and strong. Without it, bones become weak and crack easily. Kids need lots of calcium to build strong bones for life!'

example.problem: What happens if kids don't drink milk?
example.solution: Without calcium, bones become weak. They may break easily or curve. Adults who had calcium-poor childhoods suffer bone diseases.

slides.inSimpleWords: Calcium is the skeleton's best friend!

slides.title: Healthy Fats and Oils
slides.storyContext: Priya opens a small bottle of sesame oil. 'Some fats are healthy! Nuts, seeds, and oils help our brain and heart. But too much fried food is bad.'

points.label: Good fats
points.text: Healthy fats from nuts, seeds, fish, olive oil—help brain and heart. Avoid too much fried food.

slides.inSimpleWords: Some fats are healthy if you don't overeat!

slides.title: Making a Healthy Plate
slides.storyContext: Priya and Ravi draw a plate. 'Half should be vegetables and fruits. One quarter grains. One quarter protein. Plus milk!' A perfect healthy meal!

points.label: Plate model
points.text: Half: veggies/fruits. Quarter: grains. Quarter: protein. Plus dairy.

slides.inSimpleWords: A healthy plate is colorful and balanced!

image.alt: Making a Healthy Plate — Healthy Food

slides.title: Proportions Matter
slides.storyContext: Ravi makes a plate with only rice. Priya shakes her head. 'Not balanced! You need vegetables for vitamins, protein to grow, and fruit for immunity. All together in right portions!'

points.label: Balance
points.text: Each meal should have all food groups in the right amounts.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat a rainbow on every plate!

slides.title: Unhealthy vs Healthy
slides.storyContext: Priya shows two meals. 'This one has candy, chips, soda—lots of sugar. Not good! This one has rice, vegetables, lentils—much better!'

example.problem: Why is candy unhealthy?
example.solution: Candy has too much sugar and not enough nutrients. Eating too much makes teeth bad and causes sickness.

slides.inSimpleWords: Too much sugar and junk food makes us sick!

slides.title: Water for Hydration
slides.storyContext: Priya fills a glass with water. 'Water is the most important drink! Drink plenty daily to stay healthy. It's better than sugary juices!'

points.label: Water
points.text: Drink 6-8 glasses of water daily. Water is best for health!

slides.inSimpleWords: Water is the healthiest drink!

slides.title: Why Hydration Matters
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'Our bodies are 60% water! Water carries nutrients, removes waste, keeps joints moving, and helps digestion. Dehydration makes us tired and sick.'

points.label: Body's water
points.text: Water makes up most of our body. It's essential for every function.

slides.inSimpleWords: Water runs our entire body!

slides.title: Ravi's Healthy Day
slides.storyContext: Breakfast: oats and milk. Lunch: rice, dal, vegetables. Snack: apple and yogurt. Dinner: roti and paneer. 'This day will keep me strong!' says Ravi.

points.label: Sample day
points.text: Eating healthy at every meal keeps energy high and body strong.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eating healthy all day keeps us strong!

slides.title: Portion Sizes Matter
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats too much rice. Priya explains, 'Even healthy food in huge amounts makes you overweight. Portions must be right—not too little, not too much!'

points.label: Control portions
points.text: Healthy eating includes eating the right amount, not just the right foods.

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat healthy foods in healthy amounts!

slides.title: Sugar and Salt: The Dangers
slides.storyContext: Priya warns Ravi: 'Too much sugar causes obesity and dental cavities. Too much salt raises blood pressure. Keep both to minimum!'

points.label: Excess nutrients
points.text: Sugar damages teeth and causes weight gain. Salt can damage heart and kidneys. Limit both.

slides.inSimpleWords: Too much sugar and salt hurts our health!

slides.title: Digestion: Food's Journey
slides.storyContext: Priya explains, 'When you swallow food, it travels down into your stomach and intestines. Your body breaks it down into tiny nutrients that enter your blood.'

points.label: Digestion process
points.text: Food enters mouth, travels to stomach, then intestines. Nutrients are absorbed into blood.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your body turns food into fuel!

slides.title: Fiber for Digestion
slides.storyContext: Ravi eats an apple with skin. Priya says, 'Fiber in vegetables, fruits, and grains helps your digestion move smoothly. It's like a broom for your intestines!'

points.label: Fiber
points.text: Found in vegetables, fruits, and whole grains. Helps digestion and keeps you regular.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fiber is nature's digestive broom!

slides.title: Read a Food Label
slides.storyContext: Priya shows Ravi a cereal box. 'Look here—calories, carbs, protein, fiber. Understanding labels helps you choose healthier foods!'

example.problem: How do we know if a food is healthy?
example.solution: Check the label! Look for low sugar, high fiber, and nutrients. Compare similar products.

slides.inSimpleWords: Food labels tell us what's inside!

slides.title: Snacking Smart
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches Ravi: 'Snacks can be healthy! Nuts, yogurt, fruit are good snacks. Chips and candy are not. Smart snacking keeps energy steady between meals.'

points.label: Healthy snacks
points.text: Nuts, fruit, yogurt, cheese—give lasting energy. Avoid sugary and fried snacks.

slides.inSimpleWords: Snack smart, stay strong!

slides.title: Healthy Food Lesson
slides.storyContext: Ravi now understands: every food has a job. Grains for energy, proteins for growth, veggies for health, fruits for immunity, water for life!

points.label: Summary
points.text: 1. Grains = energy. 2. Proteins = growth. 3. Vegetables = vitamins. 4. Fruits = immunity. 5. Dairy = strong bones. 6. Healthy fats = brain. 7. Water = hydration. 8. Fiber = digestion. 9. Eat colorful, balanced meals! 10. Control portions. 11. Limit sugar and salt. 12. Healthy eating = healthy life!

slides.inSimpleWords: Eat healthy to grow strong and happy!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Big and Small Letter Quest
hook: Arun and Maya discover when to use big (capital) and small letters!

slides.title: Big Letters are Called CAPITALS
slides.storyContext: At school, the teacher shows Arun and Maya a big 'A' and a small 'a' on the board.

points.label: Capital Letter
points.text: The BIG letter form is called a CAPITAL letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Big letters are called CAPITAL letters!

image.alt: Big Letters are Called CAPITALS — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Every Sentence Starts with Capital
slides.storyContext: Maya reads: 'My name is Maya.' Arun points to the big 'M' at the start!

points.label: Rule 1
points.text: Every sentence ALWAYS starts with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Start sentences with a BIG capital letter!

image.alt: Every Sentence Starts with Capital — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Names Get Capital Letters
slides.storyContext: Arun writes his name: ARUN. Maya writes hers: MAYA. They use capitals!

points.label: Rule 2
points.text: Names of people ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Names start with capital letters always!

image.alt: Names Get Capital Letters — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Places Need Capitals Too
slides.storyContext: Maya says 'I live in Delhi.' Arun says 'I live in Mumbai.' Both cities start with capitals!

points.label: Rule 3
points.text: Names of places ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: City and country names start with capitals!

image.alt: Places Need Capitals Too — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Days and Months Need Capitals
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'Monday is the first day.' Maya says 'January is the first month.' Both use capitals!

points.label: Rule 4
points.text: Days and months ALWAYS start with a capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Days and months start with big capital letters!

image.alt: Days and Months Need Capitals — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Capital or Small Letter?
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya play a game: when do we use capitals?

example.problem: Write: i like eating apples on monday
example.solution: I like eating apples on Monday. (Start + name 'I' + day 'Monday' need capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Capital at start, names, places, days, months!

image.alt: Capital or Small Letter? — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Small Letters for Most Words
slides.storyContext: Maya explains: most words use small letters in the middle of a sentence!

points.label: Rule 5
points.text: Words in the middle of sentences use SMALL letters

slides.inSimpleWords: Use small letters for most words in a sentence!

image.alt: Small Letters for Most Words — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: Capital and Small Letters
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya write their 'Capital Letter Rules' poster!

points.label: Use CAPITALS for
points.text: Start of sentence, names, places, days, months

points.label: Use SMALL for
points.text: Most other words in the middle

slides.inSimpleWords: Capitals at start, names, places. Smalls for others!

image.alt: Capital and Small Letters — Capital and Small Letters

slides.title: What is a Capital Letter?
slides.storyContext: Let's understand what makes a letter 'capital' or 'small.'

points.label: Capital (uppercase)
points.text: Large, bigger size: A B C D E F G H I J K

points.label: Small (lowercase)
points.text: Small, regular size: a b c d e f g h i j k

slides.inSimpleWords: Capital letters are BIGGER. Small letters are regular size.

slides.title: The Special 'I'
slides.storyContext: The word 'I' (meaning yourself) is always a capital letter, even in the middle!

points.label: Always capital
points.text: I am happy. You and I like to play.

points.label: Remember
points.text: 'I' stands alone as a capital letter, never lowercase

slides.inSimpleWords: The word 'I' is ALWAYS a capital letter!

slides.title: Fix the Capitals - Exercise 1
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya fix sentences with wrong capitals.

example.problem: arun and maya live in delhi
example.solution: Arun and Maya live in Delhi. (Names and cities start with capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Always check: start, names, places, days need capitals!

slides.title: Fix the Capitals - Exercise 2
slides.storyContext: Maya's turn: more sentences to fix!

example.problem: i go to school on monday
example.solution: I go to school on Monday. (Both 'I' and 'Monday' need capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Remember 'I' and day names always get capitals!

slides.title: Write Your Own Sentence
slides.storyContext: Arun challenges Maya: write a sentence using at least one capital letter rule!

points.label: Your turn
points.text: Write about yourself (use 'I'), a friend (capitalize name), and a day (capitalize day)

slides.inSimpleWords: Write a sentence: I + name + day (all with capitals!)

slides.title: Titles Always Start with Capital
slides.storyContext: Maya reads a book titled 'The Adventures of Little Prince.' Every main word starts with capital!

points.label: Book and movie titles
points.text: Important words in titles start with capitals

slides.inSimpleWords: Book titles and movie names use capitals for big words!

slides.title: Practice with Real Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya check real examples from their textbooks.

example.problem: the cat sat on saturday
example.solution: The cat sat on Saturday. (Start word and day name need capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Check every sentence: first word and special words!

slides.title: When NOT to Use Capitals
slides.storyContext: Understanding what doesn't need capitals helps avoid mistakes!

points.label: No capitals for
points.text: Regular action words (run, jump, play) in the middle

points.label: No capitals for
points.text: Colors, animals, foods (unless at start): red, dog, apple

slides.inSimpleWords: Don't use capitals for regular action words!

slides.title: Spot the Mistake
slides.storyContext: Maya finds sentences with wrong capital letters. Can you fix them?

points.label: Wrong
points.text: I like Playing Football On Tuesday

points.label: Right
points.text: I like playing football on Tuesday

slides.inSimpleWords: Only START and special words get capitals!

slides.title: Countries and Cities
slides.storyContext: Arun says 'I live in India.' Maya says 'I live in Bangalore.' All place names start with capitals!

points.label: Countries
points.text: India, France, Japan, Brazil (always capital)

points.label: Cities
points.text: Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Pune (always capital)

slides.inSimpleWords: All country and city names start with capitals!

slides.title: Months Matter
slides.storyContext: Arun writes: 'I was born in March.' Let's see all the months!

example.problem: january, february, march, april
example.solution: January, February, March, April (all month names start with capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every month name starts with a capital letter!

slides.title: Days of the Week
slides.storyContext: Maya lists all seven days. Every one starts with a capital!

points.label: The seven days
points.text: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday

points.label: Always capital
points.text: Every day of the week needs a big letter

slides.inSimpleWords: All day names start with capital letters!

slides.title: Fill the Blank
slides.storyContext: Can you complete these sentences with capital letters where needed?

points.label: Question 1
points.text: My friend _____ was born on _____. (name + day)

points.label: Question 2
points.text: _____ is a country in Asia. (country name)

slides.inSimpleWords: Use capitals for names, days, and countries!

slides.title: Exclamation and Questions
slides.storyContext: Arun exclaims 'Wow!' Maya asks 'Really?' Both start with capitals even with special marks!

points.label: After ! or ?
points.text: If next sentence starts, use capital letter

slides.inSimpleWords: Even after ! or ? the next sentence starts with a capital!

slides.title: Dialogue Practice
slides.storyContext: Arun and Maya have a conversation. Each sentence starts with capital!

example.problem: arun said 'hello!' maya replied 'hi there!'
example.solution: Arun said 'Hello!' Maya replied 'Hi there!' (names and dialogue start with capitals)

slides.inSimpleWords: In conversations, every sentence and name has capitals!

slides.title: The Grammar Rule Summary
slides.storyContext: A complete list of when capitals are used.

points.label: Always use capitals
points.text: Start of sentence, names, places, days, months, 'I'

points.label: Most other words
points.text: Use small (lowercase) letters in the middle

slides.inSimpleWords: Capitals: first word, names, places, days, months, and 'I'!

slides.title: Create Your Masterpiece Sentence
slides.storyContext: Now you write a perfect sentence with every capital rule!

points.label: Must include
points.text: A name, a day or month, and proper sentence start

slides.inSimpleWords: Write one sentence showing 3 capital letter rules!

slides.title: Arun and Maya's Big Lesson
slides.storyContext: Our friends celebrate learning all about capitals and small letters!

points.label: For every sentence
points.text: Start with a capital, use small letters mostly

points.label: For special words
points.text: Names, places, days, months, 'I' — all need capitals

points.label: Practice rule
points.text: Read your sentences aloud and check every capital!

slides.inSimpleWords: You now know when to use BIG and small letters!

subject: English
title: Arun and Maya's Punctuation Adventure
hook: Learn the magic dots and marks that help sentences tell their story!

slides.title: The Period Stops the Sentence
slides.storyContext: Arun writes 'I like rice' and puts a dot. The sentence stops here!

points.label: Period (.)
points.text: A period stops a sentence. It means the idea is complete

slides.inSimpleWords: A period (.) ends a sentence with a complete idea!

image.alt: The Period Stops the Sentence — Punctuation

slides.title: Question Marks Ask Questions
slides.storyContext: Maya asks 'Do you like tea?' and puts a curvy mark with a dot.

points.label: Question Mark (?)
points.text: A question mark ends a sentence that ASKS something

slides.inSimpleWords: Question mark (?) ends a sentence that asks!

slides.title: Exclamation Marks Show Feeling
